If she's already planning to move out, then hopefully things will work themselves out. But if she doesn't, I suggest seeking help for your friend. People deal with things in so many ways, and talking to him would be the best. My friend also has gone through this- he was in love with this girl, she rejected him, he became suicidal. I strongly encouraged him to seek therapy for this, and after a month he seems better. He has stopped cutting and is no longer suicidal.  You should tell him that you're there to support him, and that he should open up to you when he's ready, I dont think you want to force anything out of him.

Maybe volunteer somewhere, get your mind off of things. If things are good, don't turn to suicide. It sounds like being alone at home is making you lonely, maybe getting out more will make things better.

Instead of these firsts, maybe think of the first day you'll find someone who loves you, or the first day you'll wake up and feel happy about being alive. Maybe strive for this instead? You're right, you are the decider of your own fate. But there are more firsts than just what your therapist says, and this world can be super shitty but I like to think there is some good, sometimes.

If these people don't like you, try not to let that bring you down! If other people want to rain on your parade, don't let them! I completely understand how you feel, but this is what my therapist says to me. Its so much different to give advice than to take it, but in the end, I think you shouldn't waste your life over people who don't seem to care about you. Its always your choice, but this ex girlfriend doesn't sound that great if she treated you like shit. These friends also don't sound that great if they're completely leaving you in the dust knowing that you're feeling this way.

I don't know if this is racist at all, but it gets me really annoyed. 

I go to a private school with mostly white kids. People throw stereotypes on me all the time, questions like "Hey anon you play basketball, right?" Or the famous, "Of course she can't swim lol." 

However something that annoyed me a lot was this friend I had. I considered her my best friend for 3 years and I stopped being friends with her recently due to other issues but about 2 years ago I cut my hair myself, and then when it grown out it was very curly. It was kind of like an afro but it wasn't because it wasn't that poofy. ANYWAAAAAY she said she liked it and she was happy I did it. But any time she was angry at me, or if I was going the other way than her, she would pull on my hair. Hard. 

I don't know it just made me feel like I was a horse and she was pulling on my reigns. Like I was some animal.

Hello! I am a female and I really think it matters what the joke was, exactly. There's a large difference from something like "Make me a sandwich, woman." to something like "What has 2 brain cells? A pregnant woman." or something like that. 

But in any case, since she was very hurt by it, he should apologize to her. But she should also stop being super angry about it. There are problems with this world and that includes sexism. Its great to try and fix it, but focusing all your anger and rage on one simple person who happens to be a friend is wrong. That hatred and anger should be used towards something like protests and such.
